input: One checked typed Enum declaration from the reconciled exact field model.
output: One native public Rust enum with unit or explicitly typed payload variants, private construction only where a payload requires it, total explicit wire emission, fallible explicit wire parsing for unit variants, and deterministic crate/module metadata.
identity: The qualified DomainSpec selector and typed-sum contract digest bind the generated module. Variant identity remains the declared variant name and ontology selector; source order is preserved in the descriptor and native declaration.
equality_and_hash: Rust PartialEq, Eq and Hash cover the enum discriminant and complete payload. No entity identity rule is inferred for payload values.
ownership: Payloads are owned by enum values. Wire parsing borrows the input string and returns an owned enum value or an owned structured error.
failure: Unknown wire values, invalid portable identifiers, stale checked fields, unsupported scalar widths, conflicting output paths and module collisions reject before publication.
effects: Generation is pure and emits planned bytes only. Generated emit and parse functions perform no I/O, environment access or mutation.
non_effects: This contract does not validate Value Object or Entity invariants, resolve references, execute Operations, publish Events, select a runtime provider, admit a profile or release a package.
counterexamples: Deriving only PartialEq while omitting Eq or Hash.
Representing a unit Enum as string constants.
Accepting an unknown wire value as a default variant.
Narrowing UInt64 through a signed integer.
Cloning a borrowed payload into a different concept type.
Claiming payload JSON decoding when only unit wire parsing is generated.
verification: Independent source observation of enum, traits, variants and explicit match arms.
Cargo compilation of generated crate and module wiring.
Native round-trip execution for every unit variant and structured rejection of unknown wire values.
Compile-fail controls for wrong payload type and private/module visibility drift.
